intro: This course covered how good communication works, the barriers that block it, and practical ways to communicate well with every person you support.
points: Keep records and shared information confidential under the UK GDPR, sharing only with those who need to know for safe care.
Communication is a two-way cycle that relies on feedback — check understanding rather than assuming your message got through.
Use both verbal and non-verbal signals, keep your words and body language matching, and read the other person's cues too.
Active listening means full attention, no interrupting, and allowing pauses so people have time to think and respond.
Spot barriers — noise, sensory loss, language, emotion — and adapt the setting, your approach, and any aids or interpreters.
Find out how each person prefers to communicate, meet the Accessible Information Standard, and record clear, factual, timely notes.
